column1: # The edge costs of the segmentation lattice (spec/words.md, LEX-6720, LEX-6721). A path costs the sum of its edges; the cheapest path wins, and a tie keeps the order of the word search. Every value is set by hand.

column3: a particle spelled in kana costs nothing more than its word
a word of one kanji is often a loose kanji of a compound
a content word of one hiragana is often a piece of a kana word
a dictionary word of three or more katakana, in place of word: a loan word is one word
a dictionary word of one katakana, or a proper noun of two, inside a longer katakana run is often a piece cut by chance
one katakana no word covers, read by its sound
a proper noun row of the base dictionary not in katakana reads a name by chance
a reading of the name layer reads a name by chance
a kana spelling of a kanji word is that word
a verb or adjective stem with no ending matched
a whole katakana run read by its sound is one word
and each katakana of it, so a long run read by sound costs more than its words
a run of Latin letters is one word and is not cut
a ー alone at the start or the end of a katakana run is a mark (a dash or a stretch), not a word
